name: Apple iPod (1st Gen)
details: The original iPod featured a mechanical scroll wheel, a 5GB 1.8-inch hard drive, FireWire connectivity, and held '1,000 songs in your pocket'.

name: Sony PlayStation Portable (PSP-1000)
details: A portable powerhouse featuring console-quality graphics, a gorgeous 4.3-inch 16:9 LCD screen, and high-tech UMD optical discs.

name: Sony PlayStation 2 (PS2 Slim)
details: The sleek redesign of the world's best-selling console, equipped with built-in Ethernet, a quiet top-loading disc tray, and an ultra-thin footprint.

name: Apple iMac G3 (Indigo / Ruby)
details: The iconic translucent all-in-one desktop that brought vibrant colors back to computing with its CRT display, slot-loading CD drive, and matching hockey-puck mouse.

name: Sony Walkman D-EJ001
details: A classic circular portable CD player featuring Sony G-Protection anti-skip technology and CD-R/RW playback support.

name: Sony VAIO PCG-C1 PictureBook
details: An ultra-portable subnotebook featuring a 180-degree built-in Motion Eye swivel webcam on top of its ultra-wide screen.

name: Apple iPhone (1st Gen / 2G)
details: Steve Jobs introduced this game-changer featuring a revolutionary multi-touch glass screen, iPod integration, and an iconic brushed-aluminum back panel.

name: Nintendo Game Boy Advance SP
details: The definitive GBA redesign featuring a clamshell body, a built-in front-lit LCD screen, and a built-in rechargeable lithium-ion battery.

name: Sony PlayStation 3 (Launch 'Fat' Model)
details: The original piano-black monster featuring a chrome trim front, slot-loading Blu-ray drive, built-in PS2 hardware emotion engine backward compatibility, and touch-sensitive power buttons.

name: Nokia 3310
details: Legendary for its indestructible build quality, replaceable Xpress-on covers, built-in custom ringtone composer, and the iconic Snake II game.

name: Apple iPod Mini (1st Gen)
details: Introduced the famous Click Wheel interface in five metallic anodized aluminum colors, powered by a tiny 1-inch Microdrive hard disk.

name: Sony Cyber-shot DSC-F707
details: A futuristic digicam featuring a massive Carl Zeiss lens housing that swiveled independently from the camera body, plus NightShot infrared shooting.

name: Sony Walkman NW-HD1
details: Sony's premium response to the iPod, built with a ultra-durable magnesium body, a backlit blue OLED display, and a 20GB hard drive.

name: Apple iBook G3 'Dual USB'
details: Shifted away from the translucent clamshell design toward an ultra-clean, minimalist white translucent polycarbonate casing.

name: Motorola RAZR V3
details: An iconic ultra-slim clamshell flip phone engineered with aircraft-grade aluminum casing and an electroluminescent keypad.

name: Apple iPod Classic (5th Gen / 5.5G Video)
details: The first iPod to play full-motion video clips and TV shows on a crisp 2.5-inch color screen, highly sought after for its warm Cirrus Logic DAC sound.

name: Nintendo DS (Original 'Fat')
details: A dual-screen handheld game console featuring an innovative bottom resistive touch screen, built-in microphone, and wireless PictoChat.

name: Sony VAIO VGN-UX180P
details: A sci-fi Micro PC featuring a 4.5-inch touch screen that slid up to reveal a full physical QWERTY keyboard, running full Windows XP.

name: Fujifilm FinePix F601 Zoom
details: A stylish, vertically-oriented brushed aluminum digicam powered by Fujifilm's unique Super CCD sensor technology.

name: Apple iPod Nano (1st Gen)
details: An impossibly thin flash-memory music player that replaced the iPod Mini, famously unveiled by Steve Jobs pulling it out of his jeans watch pocket.

name: Canon IXUS 285 / PowerShot SD Series
details: Compact, metallic credit-card-sized digicams celebrated for their rich color science, optical viewfinders, and retro CCD sensor aesthetic.

name: Sony Ericsson W800i Walkman Phone
details: The first mobile phone branded under the legendary Walkman name, complete with a dedicated music button, orange accents, and a 2MP camera.

name: Apple PowerMac G4 Cube
details: A 7-inch square computer suspended in an acrylic glass housing, featuring a top slot-loading DVD drive and silent fanless cooling.

name: Sony PSP Go (PSP-N1000)
details: A sleek, digital-only portable console with a slide-out controller pad, Bluetooth support, and 16GB built-in flash storage.

name: Apple iPod Shuffle (2nd Gen)
details: A tiny, wearable aluminum clip device with no screen, designed exclusively for randomized audio playback on the go.

name: Nintendo GameCube
details: A compact, indigo cube-shaped home console featuring a built-in top carrying handle and proprietary mini optical discs.

name: Sony VAIO X505
details: An ultra-thin laptop crafted from carbon fiber that tapered down to less than 0.38 inches thick, weighing under 1.8 lbs.

name: Nokia N-Gage
details: A taco-shaped hybrid gaming phone that combined Symbian OS mobile capabilities with physical game card cartridges.

name: Apple iMac G4 (Flat Panel)
details: Nicknamed the 'iLamp', featuring a hemispherical dome base attached to a floating LCD screen mounted on a smooth chrome swivel neck.

name: Sony Walkman NW-E507 / 'Perfume Bottle'
details: A glass-like jewel MP3 player with a hidden blue OLED display that glowed from beneath the metallic shell.

name: T-Mobile Sidekick II / III
details: The ultimate messaging phone featuring a screen that swiveled 180 degrees to reveal a full tactile QWERTY keyboard beneath.

name: Apple iPod Touch (1st Gen)
details: Offered the iPhone's revolutionary multi-touch interface, Safari web browser, and cover flow without needing a cellular contract.

name: Sony Cyber-shot DSC-T1
details: An ultra-thin metal digicam featuring a sliding front lens cover plate and a folded optical inner lens zoom mechanism.

name: Apple iPhone 3GS
details: Featuring a glossy black or white curved polycarbonate rear shell, video recording, voice control, and twice the speed of its predecessor.

name: Sony VAIO P-Series Pocket PC
details: An ultra-wide lifestyle mini notebook built to fit inside an inside jacket pocket, featuring a high-res 8-inch screen and trackpoint button.

name: Kodak FunSaver 35 Digital / EasyShare Series
details: Early digicams that docked directly onto desktop printer stands to print photos with a single physical button press.

name: Apple iPod Nano (3rd Gen 'Fatty')
details: A squarish, compact aluminum iPod featuring a wider 2-inch screen for playing video clips, nicknamed the 'Fatty'.

name: Sony Discman D-NE10
details: One of the thinnest CD/MP3 Walkman players ever constructed, housed inside an ultra-sleek magnesium alloy casing.

name: Nintendo Game Boy Micro
details: A miniature metal Game Boy Advance weighing just 2.8 ounces, featuring interchangeable faceplates and a super-bright backlit screen.

name: Apple PowerBook G4 Titanium
details: The pioneering pro laptop featuring a pure titanium enclosure, a slot-loading DVD drive, and a widescreen display.

name: Sony Cyber-shot DSC-M1
details: A hybrid video camera/digicam with a unique side-swiveling LCD screen designed to record high-quality MPEG-4 video clips.

name: Palm Pilot V / Vx
details: The gold-standard handheld PDA featuring a slim anodized aluminum body, Graffiti pen input, and monochrome LCD.

name: Apple iPod Shuffle (1st Gen)
details: Resembled a pack of chewing gum with a built-in USB cap, working directly as an external flash thumb drive.

name: Sony PlayStation Portable Slim (PSP-2000)
details: A lighter, slimmer PSP overhaul with double the system RAM, improved LCD response times, and TV-out video streaming support.

name: Microsoft Zune 30GB
details: Microsoft's bold iPod competitor featuring a double-shot translucent casing, a large portrait screen, and wireless song-sharing.

name: Nokia 7280 'Lipstick Phone'
details: A fashion-forward phone with a sliding camera mechanism, a mirror display screen, and a rotary dial wheel instead of a keypad.

name: Apple MacBook Pro (15-inch Original)
details: Replaced the PowerBook line with Intel processors, introducing the magnetic MagSafe power connector and ambient backlit keyboard.

name: Sony Walkman NW-Bean
details: A bean-shaped MP3 player built with an ergonomic hand grip, pop-up USB plug, and an invisible single-line OLED display.

name: Casio Exilim EX-M1
details: An ultra-thin credit-card camera built with a wearable metal shell, built-in MP3 player, and crisp CCD sensor.

name: Apple iPod Classic (6th/7th Gen 160GB)
details: The pinnacle of hard-drive iPods, featuring an all-aluminum anodized front face plate, cover flow view, and massive storage.

name: Sony PlayStation Vita
details: Features dual analog thumbsticks, a brilliant 5-inch OLED touch display, a rear touchpad, and high-performance handheld graphics.

name: BlackBerry Pearl 8100
details: Shrank the business smartphone down to consumer size, featuring a translucent trackball, SureType QWERTY keyboard, and email sync.

name: Apple iBook G3 Clamshell
details: Vibrant translucent laptops featuring integrated carrying handles, rubberized side bumpers, and pop-out wireless Airport cards.

name: Sony Ericsson T610
details: A two-tone aluminum-and-black candybar phone that popularized built-in digital cameras and 65,000-color screens.

name: Nintendo Wii
details: A compact white console featuring motion-sensing Wii Remotes, blue-glowing optical drive slot, and system Mii avatars.

name: Sony Walkman NWZ-W202
details: A futuristic cord-free wearable MP3 player shaped like a headset that snapped together magnetically around your neck.

name: Apple iPod Nano (5th Gen)
details: Packed a glossy polished aluminum finish, an FM radio tuner, a built-in microphone speaker, and a video camera into a tiny frame.

name: Sony Cyber-shot DSC-R1
details: A bridge camera featuring a massive APS-C sensor paired with a fixed Carl Zeiss zoom lens and top-mounted LCD display.

name: Nokia 8800
details: A luxury slider phone built with a full stainless-steel body, reinforced scratch-resistant glass, and smooth ball-bearing slide action.

name: Sony VAIO VGN-AR11S
details: The world's first laptop equipped with a built-in Blu-ray Disc recordable drive and a 17-inch 1080p full HD display.

name: Apple MacBook Air (1st Gen)
details: Steve Jobs famously slid this impossibly thin aluminum laptop out of a standard manila office envelope at Macworld.

name: Creative Nomad Jukebox Zen Xtra
details: A heavy-duty hard drive audio player with an blue backlit display that competed head-to-head with early iPods.

name: Sony Walkman NW-A800
details: The first video Walkman MP3 player, housed in a thin metallic chassis with crystal-clear color video screen rendering.

name: Leica D-Lux 2
details: A high-end compact digicam with a classic retro design, 16:9 native aspect ratio sensor, and Leica DC Vario-Elmar optical lens.

name: Apple iPod Nano (6th Gen)
details: A square, touch-screen clip device that inspired early smartwatch mods using aftermarket wrist straps.

name: Sony Cyber-shot DSC-G1
details: A sliding digicam equipped with a huge 3.5-inch high-res LCD screen and built-in Wi-Fi for album sharing.

name: Microsoft Xbox 360 (S - Slim)
details: Redesigned with a matte/gloss black shell, whisper-quiet internal fan, touch buttons, and integrated Wi-Fi.

name: Sony VAIO W-Series Netbook
details: A colorful mini-laptop crafted with textured palm rests and an isolated chicklet keyboard for portable computing.

name: HP iPAQ hx4700
details: A flagship Pocket PC featuring a magnesium body, a VGA screen, double card slots, and a unique touchpad controller.

name: Nokia N95
details: The ultimate smartphone before touchscreens took over, featuring a two-way slide design, 5MP Carl Zeiss optics, and built-in GPS.

name: Apple iPod Shuffle (3rd Gen)
details: An ultra-tiny aluminum bar with no physical buttons at all, completely controlled using inline headphone buttons and VoiceOver speech.

name: Sony Walkman NW-S203F
details: A cylindrical, water-resistant aluminum fitness MP3 player with a built-in step counter and hidden single-line screen.

name: Olympus Camedia C-700 Ultra Zoom
details: A compact bridge camera known for squeezing a massive 10x optical glass zoom lens into a lightweight body.

name: HTC Touch Diamond
details: A Windows Mobile smartphone featuring a geometric faceted rear back cover and the custom 3D TouchFLO UI interface.

name: Apple Cinema Display (23-inch HD)
details: Sleek aluminum widescreen monitors with ultra-thin bezels that set the standard for pro creative workspaces.

name: Sony PSP-3000
details: The ultimate PSP revision featuring an upgraded wide-color-gamut LCD screen with anti-glare technology and a built-in microphone.

name: BlackBerry Bold 9000
details: Features a leather-textured back cover, a metallic side rim, a crisp display, and the most celebrated physical QWERTY keyboard.

name: Ricoh GR Digital (1st Gen)
details: A cult-favorite compact camera featuring a fast 28mm equivalent prime lens, magnesium alloy body, and street-photography ergonomics.

name: Sony VAIO VGN-FS Series
details: Popularized Sony's dual-lamp XBRITE glossy displays for vibrant contrast during DVD playback.

name: Apple iPod Mini (2nd Gen)
details: Upgraded with richer anodized aluminum colors, laser-engraved hard drive capacity markings, and extended 18-hour battery life.

name: LG Chocolate (KG800)
details: A slick slider phone with a hidden red touch-sensitive pad that illuminated through its dark casing like melting chocolate.

name: Sony Walkman Bean NW-E307
details: Ergonomic, colorful bean-shaped MP3 player featuring a built-in USB jack that popped open with a twist dial.

name: Samsung YP-P2
details: An iPod touch competitor with a 3-inch widescreen touch LCD, Bluetooth 2.0 audio streaming, and a thin metal shell.

name: Nintendo DSi
details: Slimmer DS revision that added two built-in VGA digital cameras, a SD card slot, and downloadable DSiWare games.

name: Apple Time Capsule
details: A Wi-Fi router containing an integrated server hard drive designed for wireless Apple Time Machine desktop backups.

name: Sony Cyber-shot DSC-TX1
details: An ultra-thin sliding digital camera featuring an Exmor R CMOS sensor for low-light shots and touch-screen controls.

name: Motorola MOTO ROKR E1
details: The first phone integrated with Apple iTunes software, featuring built-in stereo speakers and a dedicated music key.

name: Sony VAIO VGN-FW Series
details: Features a 16.4-inch 16:9 widescreen display and built-in Blu-ray optical disc drive for portable cinema playback.

name: Samsung Yepp YP-55
details: A tubular MP3 player with a blue-backlit screen and a twistable USB cap connector.

name: Panasonic Lumix DMC-LX3
details: A legendary enthusiast compact digicam featuring a ultra-wide Leica f/2.0 lens and physical aspect ratio switches.

name: Apple iPod Photo
details: The first iPod with a full-color LCD display capable of displaying photo slide shows alongside music artwork.

name: Sony Ericsson Xperia X1
details: Features an arc-sliding QWERTY keyboard, brushed steel panels, and custom 3D panel interfaces.

name: Nokia 7380 (L'Amour Collection)
details: A pen-shaped phone built with etched leather, amber mirror glass, and a fabric label tag.

name: Sony Walkman NWZ-A845
details: An ultra-slim 7.2mm Walkman MP3 player featuring a high-contrast OLED display and built-in digital noise-canceling hardware.

name: Alienware Area-51 m5550
details: A heavy-duty gaming laptop featuring glowing alien logos, customizable lighting zones, and desktop-class graphics power.

name: Apple LED Cinema Display (24-inch)
details: An aluminum and glass display equipped with an integrated iSight camera, stereo speakers, and a multi-headed MagSafe cable.

name: Sony Cyber-shot DSC-U10
details: An ultra-tiny pocket digicam that turned on instantly by sliding open its front protective lens shield.

name: Flip Video UltraHD
details: A pocket video camera featuring a flip-out USB connector and simple one-touch red button recording controls.

name: Sony VAIO VGN-TT Series
details: An 11-inch subnotebook constructed with carbon fiber, featuring a built-in Blu-ray burner drive and dual-channel SSD storage.

name: Apple iPod Classic (4th Gen / Click Wheel)
details: The landmark model that integrated the iPod Mini's Click Wheel onto the full-size grayscale iPod model for the first time.

name: Casio Databank DBC-32
details: The ultimate Y2K calculator watch featuring a 10-key physical keypad, 25-page databank memory, multi-language support, and a high-contrast digital display.

name: Fossil BigTic (Matrix / Flame Animated)
details: An iconic hybrid watch featuring analog hands over a full-screen liquid crystal background that constantly animated running seconds in futuristic Y2K digital fonts.

name: Nike Triax Armフォー (Triax Series)
details: Featuring an iconic asymmetrical organic plastic case designed to tilt toward the runner's eye, with high-contrast lap timers and futuristic Y2K ergonomics.

name: Casio G-Shock DW-6900 'Translucent Clear'
details: A staple of early 2000s streetwear featuring a clear jelly resin casing, triple-graph LCD display, and electro-luminescent (EL) backlight.

name: Timex Datalink USB
details: An early wearable computer watch co-developed with Microsoft that synced calendar events, contacts, and alarms directly via a USB computer connection.

name: Fossil Wrist PDA (FX2001)
details: A miniature Palm OS computer worn on the wrist, featuring a 160x160 monochrome touch screen, tiny stylus, and virtual Graffiti handwriting recognition.

name: Casio Baby-G BG-160 Translucent Series
details: A pop-culture Y2K icon featuring vibrant translucent gel straps, protective wire face guards, and animated LCD mascot clips when the backlight was pressed.

name: Suunto Vector HR
details: The definitive outdoor adventure watch of the era, packing a digital compass, altimeter, barometer, and distinct bubble-level housing.

name: Seiko Spoon (Spoon Digital Series)
details: A cult-classic Y2K design from Seiko featuring a fluid, metallic futuristic shell and an integrated curved LCD screen.

name: Oakley Time Bomb / D1 Digital
details: Sculpted from lightweight titanium and high-tech rubbers, featuring futuristic organic industrial design signatures unique to Oakley's 2000s lineup.

name: Casio ProTrek PRG-40
details: A rugged triple-sensor altimeter/barometer watch equipped with a massive dual-layer LCD matrix screen for real-time terrain navigation.

name: Diesel DZ-9016 Animated Digital
details: Featuring an oversized industrial stainless steel block casing with a sunken digital matrix screen rendering retro-futuristic typography.

name: Puma Sport Digital Curve
details: A sleek, wrap-around rubberized sports watch built with a continuous curved LCD screen and bold Y2K neon colorways.

name: Casio G-Shock Mudman G-9000
details: Engineered with dual 1/100th second stopwatches, low-temperature resistance, and fully sealed mud-resistant rubber pushers.

name: Timex Ironman Ironman Sleek 50-Lap
details: The classic training watch featuring a curved metallic bezel, distinct top-mounted split button, and Indiglo night-light illumination.

name: Adidas Response Digital Runner
details: An ergonomic, ventilated running watch with a angled digital face for quick viewing on the wrist during long-distance training.

name: Nixon The Newton Digital
details: A minimalist, playful digital watch encased in a seamless molded silicone band with a dot-matrix digital time presentation.

name: Casio Futurist LA-200
details: Compact, metallic Cyber-Y2K dress watches featuring mirrored faceplates, pastel LCD displays, and sleek integrated steel bracelets.

name: Fossil Starchung / Animated OLED Digital
details: Early experimentation with bright organic LED displays, showcasing custom glowing digital fonts and screensaver animations.

name: Tokyo Flash Barcode / LED Watch
details: Cryptic Japanese LED watches that displayed the time using futuristic decoded light bars, grid patterns, and geometric LED sequences.

name: Sony PocketStation
details: A tiny handheld device that doubled as a PlayStation memory card and a standalone miniature LCD gaming console.

name: Digital Photo Keychain
details: Pocket-sized keychains featuring a tiny 1.5-inch color LCD display that stored and cycled through digital photos.

name: Casio Wrist Audio Player (WMP-1V)
details: The world's first wristwatch with a built-in MP3 player, featuring a monochrome LCD display and headphone jack right on the wrist.

name: Cyiko / Pocket TV (Handheld CRT/LCD TV)
details: Portable pocket-sized televisions with telescopic antennas that pulled analog broadcast TV signals directly out of the air.

name: Sony Walkman NW-Bean
details: An ergonomic bean-shaped MP3 player built with a bright OLED display and a pop-up USB connector that clicked out with a twist dial.

name: Sony Walkman NW-S203F (Fitness Cylinder)
details: A water-resistant, tubular aluminum MP3 player with a built-in G-sensor pedometer and an invisible single-line OLED display.

name: MiniDisc (Sony MD)
details: A magneto-optical disc format enclosed in a tough plastic cartridge, offering digital audio recording and re-writable capability in a pocketable size.

name: 3.5-inch Floppy Disk
details: Holding just 1.44MB of data, these hard plastic disks were the universal standard for saving text documents and basic software before USB drives took over.

name: Sony CD-R / CD-RW Audio Discs
details: Blank 700MB compact optical discs used for burning custom MP3 music playlists or data backups using home PC disc burners.

name: Sony Memory Stick PRO Duo
details: Sony's proprietary miniature memory card format, used exclusively across PSP handhelds, Cyber-shot cameras, and Handycam camcorders.

name: CompactFlash (CF) Card
details: Thick, durable flash memory cards with exposed pin connectors, favored by professional DSLR cameras and early handheld PDAs.

name: xD-Picture Card
details: A tiny, gold-pinned memory card developed jointly by Fujifilm and Olympus for their ultra-compact digital cameras.

name: Apple 30-pin Dock Connector Cable
details: The iconic wide charging cable used across generations of classic iPods, iPhones, and iPads before Lightning cables existed.

name: 3.5mm Cassette Deck Adapter
details: A cassette tape with an aux cable attached, allowing users to play audio from portable CD players or iPods through older car tape decks.

name: USB Flash Drive (Keychain Style)
details: Early 64MB to 512MB USB thumb drives featuring removable protective caps, lanyard loops, and blinking activity LEDs.

name: Sony PlayStation 2 Memory Card (8MB)
details: The MagicGate 8MB memory card plugged into the front of the PS2, holding game saves and profile settings.

name: Nintendo GameCube Memory Card 59
details: A small plastic memory block inserted into the top of the GameCube console to save game progress across 59 data blocks.

name: Universal Media Disc (UMD)
details: Sony's 60mm optical disc enclosed in a protective plastic shell, capable of holding up to 1.8GB of games and movies for the PSP.

name: Mini DVD-R (8cm)
details: Miniature optical discs used in camcorders like the Sony Handycam, allowing users to record video directly to disc and play it in a home DVD player.

name: Pocket Cyber Pet / Tamagotchi Connection
details: Keychain virtual pets equipped with infrared ports, allowing two devices to connect wirelessly so pets could visit each other.
